summary: Introduces GUI-CC, a benchmark for assessing GUI world models as multi-step agent environments. Separate reference-action and agent-loop tracks test whether generated screens preserve context, plausible transitions, and task progress throughout interaction.

name: JarvisGUI: Towards Cross-Device GUI Agents with Dynamic Task Composition
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: JarvisGUI composes typed input-output task transformations into dynamic workflows spanning Android, Windows and Ubuntu devices. Its virtual-environment benchmark tests transfer of intermediate results, shared state and cross-device dependencies.

name: CADWorld: Computer-Use Benchmark for Long-Horizon Computer-Aided Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CADWorld evaluates screenshot-and-GUI agents on long FreeCAD workflows, from modeling and assembly to manufacturing and simulation. Executable checks inspect saved engineering artifacts for geometry, constraints, construction structure and downstream state.

name: Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: EvoSkill-GUI revises reusable skill files from execution feedback through an executor–critic loop. It studies how training-free updates to localization, recovery and procedure information help subsequent mobile and desktop tasks.

name: The Hard Part Comes After Search: Benchmarking Web Agents on Synthesizing, Organizing, and Displaying Knowledge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: KNOWS benchmarks browser workflows that retrieve and synthesize information into documents, presentations and spreadsheets. Task-specific evaluators combine deterministic checks with model judgments, distinguishing partial progress from usable end-to-end artifact completion.

name: LongPuzzleBench: Evaluating GUI Agents on Long-Horizon Visual Puzzles
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. Agents execute real GUI moves in six puzzle games; the tasks diagnose computer-control planning but remain game-based rather than general productivity workflows.
summary: LongPuzzleBench evaluates coherent long-horizon planning on persistent visual puzzle boards through native GUI actions. It compares GUI-only and code-assisted agents and uses controlled hints and memory diagnostics to examine decisions that preserve or eliminate future solutions.

name: PrecogUI: Proactive GUI Agents via Pre-cognitive Simulation and Experience Retrieval
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Presents PrecogUI, which retrieves prior anomaly and success patterns and predicts symbolic UI transitions before choosing actions. It also introduces InterfereBench, generated for evaluating long GUI workflows with disruptive events and recovery requirements.

name: AMBER: Training Long-Horizon Web Agents through Append-Only Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces AMBER, an append-only memory framework in which a web agent learns to reason, act, and retain evidence using outcome-reward reinforcement learning. It studies whether preserving entries avoids the loss of facts and corrective feedback seen with rewritten memory.

name: AgentHorizon: Evaluating Agentic Judges for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces AgentHorizon, a benchmark for judging long computer-use trajectories using closely related instructions paired with recorded actions and screenshots. It tests whether judges can detect constraint violations and distinguish successful tasks from similar but incompatible requests.

name: Adaptive-Group Process Rewards for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Groups GUI trajectories by subgoal and combines action-level and group-level assessments into intermediate rewards for training agents with sparse task outcomes.

notes: App WorkEnvs expose UI observations and interaction interfaces alongside file and tool workflows; no specific operating system or pixel-control success is established. notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces CarryOn, which maintains evidence-linked task objects and remaining-work context across history compression, with evaluations on desktop tasks and web research.

name: ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation
notes: Privileged screenshot history is used during training, while deployment retains self-generated textual state. GUI results use action/step metrics and model-specific history settings; online Sokoban transfer is separate. GRPO rewards action correctness, valid output format and compression length. Diagnostic memory replay is distinct from the validation gap used to schedule training. No independent reproduction.
summary: ECHOES learns recursive textual task memory through privileged screenshot-history distillation and GRPO, then predicts GUI actions from the current screenshot and memory.

name: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
notes: Reviewed the complete abstract and selected v1 synthesis, training and evaluation sections. The system uses hybrid GUI/MCP/CLI interfaces. Evaluation includes benchmark subsets and model-based judgments, so reported scores are not treated as directly comparable GUI-only results. No independent reproduction.
summary: WildAWM synthesizes resettable GUI/MCP/CLI environments and cross-interface tasks, using execution-based checks of solvability, difficulty and verifier consistency before supervised and reinforcement learning.
